subject: Keystore accountability and access: decision queue
messages:
From: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@medspring.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orthocare.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Audit scope details + keystore responsibilities

Hi Hannah / Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our compliance team asked for a concise matrix showing: 1) who owns key custody (Redwood vs customer BYOK), 2) which audit logs capture key access and administrative actions, and 3) the retention window for those logs (we need HIPAA-friendly retention justification).

Specific asks:
- Exportable audit evidence for key rotations (per-tenant) going back 12 months
- Confirmation of whether SSO-authenticated admin actions are recorded with user-identifiers (not just service accounts)
- If Redwood supports temporary delegated access (timebound ops) and how that appears in logs

I'm attaching the audit scope template our auditors prefer. Can you confirm what is feasible and what would require an exception? We have a procurement timeline so clarity by EOD Tuesday would be ideal.

Karen Lopez
Security & Privacy Lead
Medspring Health

Attachment: medspring_audit_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@medspring.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit scope details + keystore responsibilities

Hi Karen —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick acknowledgement: we can produce an export for key-rotation events and admin actions, but there are a few nuances to map back to your auditor template (especially around SSO identity resolution and retention policy).

To keep this actionable, I've proposed an internal triage plan below and included owners:
- Audit evidence export (per-tenant rotation history): Marcus (serving/runtime) — feasibility + estimated export format
- SSO identity mapping (admin actions show human user): Priya (auth/ops) — confirm what we log today and what would need a pipeline change
- Temporary delegated access (timebound roles): Jonas (product) — document current patterns and exception request process
- Retention window alignment and SLA notes: Hannah (security/product liaison) — confirm default retention and options for extended retention / escrow

Can the internal owners reply with short bullets and a confidence level by EOD Monday? If items require engineering work beyond docs (e.g., new telemetry export), we'll surface delivery estimates.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Hannah / team —

Quick notes from runtime side:
- Key rotation events: we log rotation events per-tenant; current export is JSON lines with fields {tenant_id, key_id, rotation_time, rotation_initiator}. I attached a small accountability matrix CSV for internal review.
- SSO user attribution: admin actions currently record the auth_subject value. If the request is done via an OAuth service account or internal operator, we record service principal ids. Mapping to an HR identity (email) depends on upstream identity provider (most customers have this mapping in SAML assertions).
- Retention: default audit log retention in hosted mode is 90 days. For Dedicated/Private customers we have options to extend via archive exports; 12-month on-demand exports are feasible but will incur storage and processing time.

Blocked / decision points:
1) Do we need to implement a transformation layer to resolve auth_subject -> human email for SSO flows? That would be a 2-sprint work (SERV-882) to add a lookup cache and export flag.
2) Do we accept an evidence delivery model (export + signed statement) instead of live 12-month retention? That could be the short-term compromise for procurement.

I'll link the design doc and a short sample export now.

Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer — Runtime

Attachment: keystore_accountability_matrix.csv (CSV, 3KB)
Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SERV-882
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karen Lopez <karen.lopez@medspring.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit scope details + keystore responsibilities

Heads-up / next steps:

- SSO identity mapping: we already surface name/id from SAML when available; for customers that don't send email in assertion we can use the audit export plus an enrichment pass from the IdP logs. Implementation path: short-term (docs + enrichment run) — owners: Priya + Marcus; ETA: 1 week for a reproducible export process.
- Temporary delegated access: product supports scoped, time-limited API tokens in Dedicated; for hosted customers we can document manual escalation flow. Jonas will draft the exception language.
- Retention options: for Medspring specifically I propose: (A) provide a 12-month point-in-time export on contract (one-time deliverable) + (B) offer an add-on for continuous 12-month retention (costed). This avoids changing default retention and meets auditors.

Action items (owners / due):
- Marcus: attach sample export CSV schema and a 1-paragraph runbook for how we produce a 12-month rotation export — due 2026-11-05
- Priya: draft SSO mapping note (limits + enrichment path) and example assertion mappings — due 2026-11-05
- Jonas: draft exception/pricing language for procurement and update the contract clause — due 2026-11-06
- Hannah: consolidate answers into the auditor template and send to Karen — due 2026-11-06

I'll produce the short notes and push to the Drive link Hannah listed.

Priya Natarajan
Product Security Manager | Redwood Inference
